chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of: from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris. And the Shaykh informed me from Ahmad ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amraki, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man wearing a tight ring, who does not know whether the water flows beneath it or not—what should he do? He said: “If he knows that the water does not enter beneath it, then he must remove it when he performs wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.الضَّيِّقُ: tight, such that it may block water from reaching the skin
key_terms.الْخَاتَمُ: a ring worn on the hand
key_terms.يَدْخُلُهُ: enters beneath it or reaches the area covered by it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing wudu (ablution) while wearing a tight ring?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution) when a person is wearing a tight ring. If one knows that water does not reach beneath the ring, it must be removed so that water reaches the skin during wudu (ablution).
